_about: NCAA Division I softball conference tournament formats, 2015-2019 and 2021-2026 (no 2020), for every D-I softball conference except ACC, Big 12, Big Ten, Pac-12 and SEC (see softball_power_conferences.md). Entries: teams = qualifiers (0 = no tournament); format single_elim|double_elim|pods|pool_play|series|none; byes = top seeds skipping the opening round (double_byes where some skip two rounds); final single|if_necessary|best_of_3; auto_bid tournament|regular_season. 'verified': true = format read from the cited source for that season; false = carried from the nearest verified season (see notes). Compiled 2026-10-27 from Wikipedia raw wikitext, conference/athletics sites, record books and NCAA pre-championship manuals.
rules_notes: CONFERENCE NOTES: (1) Big West (through 2024), West Coast (all of 2015-2026; first WCC tournament planned for 2027) and Mountain West (2007-2022) held no softball tournament; the regular-season champion took the automatic bid. The Ivy League used a best-of-3 championship series (division winners 2015-17; top two 2018, 2019, 2022), cancelled spring 2021 sports entirely, and started a 4-team double-elimination tournament in 2023. The MAC eliminated its tournament for 2021 (regular-season champion got the bid) and resumed in 2022. (2) 'byes' = seeds that skip the opening round; where some seeds skip two rounds a 'double_byes' field is added. A single-elimination play-in round in front of a double-elimination bracket is still recorded as format 'double_elim'. (3) final: 'if_necessary' = true double elimination (a second final game if the unbeaten team loses once); this is the default assumption for double-elimination brackets unless a source says the championship was a single winner-take-all game. NCAA D-I SOFTBALL CHAMPIONSHIP: Field of 64 (32 automatic qualifiers + 32 at-large through 2024; 31 AQs + 33 at-large in 2025 and 2026 per the 2024-25 and 2025-26 manuals), 16 four-team double-elimination regionals, 8 best-of-3 super regionals, 8-team WCWS. National seeds: 16 national seeds every year 2015-2025 (2018-19, 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2024-25 pre-championship manuals: 'Sixteen teams will be seeded. Each of the seeded teams will be placed at one of the regional sites and will host regional competition, provided a team bids to host and meets the hosting requirements'; 2016 example: the 16 national seeds hosted regionals, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NCAA_Division_I_softball_tournament). So the 16 regional hosts are, by rule, the 16 national seeds unless a seed did not bid or failed hosting requirements. 2026: first year the committee seeded 32 teams - top 16 ranked 1-16 (and still offered hosting), seeds 17-32 placed in four groups of eight with 1-8 pairings within each regional (https://ncaaorg.s3.amazonaws.com/championships/sports/softball/d1/2025-26D1WSB_PrechampsMnual.pdf; https://ncaaorg.s3.amazonaws.com/championships/sports/softball/d1/Aug2025D1WSB_AnnualReport.pdf; https://ncaaorg.s3.amazonaws.com/championships/sports/softball/d1/Aug2026D1WSB_AnnualReport.pdf 'first year of seeding 17 through 32 in groups of four'). Super-regional pairings 1 v 16, 2 v 15, ... 8 v 9 if seeds advance. 2015-2017 manuals were not retrieved (2014-15 and 2016-17 manual URLs return NoSuchKey); 16 seeds assumed for those years (unchanged since 2005). RPI (from the pre-championship manuals' selection criteria): 25% team winning percentage, 50% opponents' success (winning percentage), 25% opponents' strength of schedule (opponents' opponents' winning percentage), plus bonus points for wins against the top 50 and penalty points for losses against teams ranked 225 and below (2018-19 through 2024-25 manuals: https://ncaaorg.s3.amazonaws.com/championships/sports/softball/d1/2018-19D1WSB_PreChampsManual.pdf, https://ncaaorg.s3.amazonaws.com/championships/sports/softball/d1/2024-25D1WSB_PrechampsManual.pdf); the 2025-26 manual changes the bonus to wins against the top 75 and penalties to losses against 227 and below. No home/road weighting of wins is stated in any softball manual (unlike baseball's 1.3/0.7 road/home weighting since 2013, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rating_percentage_index); the NCAA softball RPI reports show Road/Neutral/Home records only as information (https://web1.ncaa.org/app_data/weeklyrpi/2019WSBrpi1.html). Treat softball RPI as unweighted 25/50/25 plus undisclosed bonus/penalty values. The committee may also consult KPI (2024-25 on) and DSR (2025-26) rankings. WCWS format: unchanged 2015-2026. Eight teams in two four-team double-elimination brackets (1v8, 4v5 | 2v7, 3v6) with a crossover: the loser of a second-round game drops into the losers' bracket on the other side. The semifinal ('bracket final') is one team with no losses against one with a loss; if the unbeaten team loses, an if-necessary game is played the same day (Monday). The two survivors play a best-of-3 championship series (since 2005), and earlier WCWS losses do not carry over (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_College_World_Series). In 2025-26 the committee discussed moving semifinal if-necessary games from Monday to the Tuesday off day to avoid doubleheaders. The 2026 report supports the change but sets no implementation date, so the format did not change through 2026 (https://ncaaorg.s3.amazonaws.com/championships/sports/softball/d1/Aug2025D1WSB_AnnualReport.pdf; https://ncaaorg.s3.amazonaws.com/championships/sports/softball/d1/Aug2026D1WSB_AnnualReport.pdf).

Big Sky.description: Top four teams in a 4-team double-elimination bracket.

Big South.description: 9 teams: 8 v 9 single-elimination play-in, then an 8-team double-elimination bracket with a single-game championship.

Big West.description: No conference tournament; the regular-season champion received the automatic bid (first Big West softball tournament was 2025).
Big West.notes: Inferred from the 2025 event being billed as the inaugural Big West Softball Championship.

CAA.description: Top four teams in a 4-team double-elimination bracket.

Horizon League.description: 6-team double elimination; top two seeds get a first-round bye, seeds 3-6 play opening-round games.

Ivy League.description: Ivy League Championship Series: best-of-three between the Lou Gehrig (South) and Red Rolfe (North) division winners.

MAAC.description: 6-team double elimination; top two seeds get a first-round bye, seeds 3-6 play opening-round games.

MEAC.description: Top four from each division (North/South), cross-division pairings (1N v 4S etc.) in an 8-team double-elimination bracket.

Mid-American.description: Top 8 teams in an 8-team double-elimination bracket at Firestone Stadium.

Missouri Valley.description: 8-team single-elimination stepladder: seeds 5-8 open, seeds 3-4 enter round 2, seeds 1-2 enter the semifinals.

Mountain West.description: No conference tournament; the regular-season champion received the automatic bid (MW held no softball tournament 2007-2022).
Mountain West.notes: MW softball tournament held 2000-06, then dropped until 2023.

NEC.description: Top four teams in a 4-team double-elimination bracket.

Ohio Valley.description: 8-team double-elimination bracket at the No. 1 seed's field.

Patriot League.description: Top four teams in a 4-team double-elimination bracket.

SWAC.description: Top four from each division (8 teams) in a double-elimination bracket at Decatur, Ala.; cross-division opening matchups.
SWAC.notes: Bracket release says only 'championship game set for Saturday'; if-necessary second game assumed (standard true double elimination, as stated in 2019 and 2022-25 releases).

Southern.description: Top 7 in a double-elimination bracket, top seed bye; the championship is a single winner-take-all game.

Southland.description: Top 6 eligible teams; seeds 3-6 open, seeds 1-2 get byes; double elimination.
Southland.notes: Abilene Christian and Incarnate Word ineligible (D-I transition).

Summit League.description: Top 6: seeds 3-6 play a single-elimination first round, then double elimination with seeds 1-2.

Sun Belt.description: 8 teams: single-elimination first round, then the 4 winners play double elimination; single winner-take-all championship game.

WAC.description: 5 teams: seeds 4 and 5 play an opening game, then double elimination with seeds 1-3.

West Coast.description: No conference tournament; the regular-season champion (with tiebreakers) received the automatic bid.
West Coast.notes: WCC announced June 2025 a 4-team double-elimination softball tournament starting in 2026-27 (i.e. spring 2027).
